desc: Read input N and permutation P.

For each index $i$ from 1 to $N-1$, calculate $C_i$, which is the count of numbers in $P[0 \dots i-1]$ (0-indexed) that are greater than $i$ (1-indexed value). Note: $P$ is 1-indexed in problem, so values are $1 \dots N$.

To compute $C_i$ efficiently for all $i$, we can use a Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree) or Segment Tree. Iterate $i$ from 1 to $N$. At step $i$, we have processed $P[1 \dots i]$. We want to count how many of these are $> i$.
Alternatively, $C_i = (\text{total elements in } P[1 \dots i]) - (\text{elements in } P[1 \dots i] \text{ that are } \le i)$.
Since there are exactly $i$ elements in $P[1 \dots i]$, $C_i = i - (\text{count of } x \in P[1 \dots i] \text{ such that } x \le i)$.
Use a Fenwick Tree to maintain the counts of values seen so far. For each $i$ from 1 to $N-1$:
Query the Fenwick Tree for the number of elements $\le i$. Let this be $K$.
Add $i \times C_i$ to the total cost.
Implement a Fenwick Tree (BIT) to handle point updates and prefix sums.
